# Renewable Energy Cost Revolution: LCOE, Capacity & Fossil Fuel Subsidies (2010–2024)

## Overview
This collection of four datasets tracks the economic transformation of the global energy sector from 2010 to 2024. It covers the declining levelized cost of energy for solar PV, onshore wind, and battery storage; the cost range of new fossil fuel generation; cumulative renewable installed capacity; and annual global fossil fuel subsidies.

## Data Source

### lcoe_trends
Annual LCOE values for three technologies: `solar_pv`, `onshore_wind`, and `battery_storage`. All values in 2023 real USD per MWh. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV ranges from 359 to 33; onshore wind from 95 to 35; battery storage from 1,100 to 102.

### fossil_fuel_lcoe_range
Biennial LCOE ranges for new-build gas CCGT (`gas_ccgt_low`, `gas_ccgt_high`) and coal (`coal_low`, `coal_high`). 8 rows at even-year intervals. Values in 2023 real USD/MWh. These define the reference band against which renewable crossover points are identified.

### installed_capacity
Cumulative global installed capacity in GW for `solar_pv_gw` and `onshore_wind_gw`. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV grows from 40 to 1,950 GW; onshore wind from 178 to 960 GW.

### fossil_fuel_subsidies
Annual global fossil fuel subsidies in nominal billion USD, split into `consumption_subsidies_bn` and `production_subsidies_bn`, with a `total_subsidies_bn` sum. 15 rows (2010–2024). Total ranges from ~290 to ~700 billion.

## Data Notes

# Renewable Energy Cost Revolution: LCOE, Capacity & Fossil Fuel Subsidies (2010–2024)

## Overview
This collection of four datasets tracks the economic transformation of the global energy sector from 2010 to 2024. It covers the declining levelized cost of energy for solar PV, onshore wind, and battery storage; the cost range of new fossil fuel generation; cumulative renewable installed capacity; and annual global fossil fuel subsidies.

## Data Source

### lcoe_trends
Annual LCOE values for three technologies: `solar_pv`, `onshore_wind`, and `battery_storage`. All values in 2023 real USD per MWh. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV ranges from 359 to 33; onshore wind from 95 to 35; battery storage from 1,100 to 102.

### fossil_fuel_lcoe_range
Biennial LCOE ranges for new-build gas CCGT (`gas_ccgt_low`, `gas_ccgt_high`) and coal (`coal_low`, `coal_high`). 8 rows at even-year intervals. Values in 2023 real USD/MWh. These define the reference band against which renewable crossover points are identified.

### installed_capacity
Cumulative global installed capacity in GW for `solar_pv_gw` and `onshore_wind_gw`. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV grows from 40 to 1,950 GW; onshore wind from 178 to 960 GW.

### fossil_fuel_subsidies
Annual global fossil fuel subsidies in nominal billion USD, split into `consumption_subsidies_bn` and `production_subsidies_bn`, with a `total_subsidies_bn` sum. 15 rows (2010–2024). Total ranges from ~290 to ~700 billion.

## Data Notes
- LCOE figures are illustrative estimates aligned with IRENA and BloombergNEF reporting trends but rounded for clarity.
- Battery storage LCOE reflects 4-hour lithium-ion systems.
- 2022 spike in fossil LCOE and subsidies reflects the global energy price crisis.
- Fossil fuel subsidy estimates cover direct government subsidies only; implicit subsidies (e.g., unpriced externalities) are excluded.
- 2024 values are preliminary estimates.

### Sequence Diagrams
**Use Mermaid.** Lifelines, messages, activation boxes, notes, and loops all need automatic layout. Use Mermaid's `sequenceDiagram` syntax. Style actors and messages via CSS overrides on `.actor`, `.messageText`, `.activation` classes.

### Data Flow Diagrams
**Use Mermaid.** Data flow diagrams emphasize connections over boxes — exactly what Mermaid excels at. Use `graph TD` (or `graph LR` for simple linear flows) with edge labels for data descriptions. Thicker, colored edges for primary flows. Source/sink nodes styled differently from transform nodes via Mermaid's `classDef`.

### Schema / ER Diagrams
**Use Mermaid.** Relationship lines between entities need automatic routing. Use Mermaid's `erDiagram` syntax with entity attributes. Style via `themeVariables` and CSS overrides on `.er.entityBox` and `.er.relationshipLine`.

### State Machines / Decision Trees
**Use Mermaid.** Use `stateDiagram-v2` for states with labeled transitions. Supports nested states, forks, joins, and notes. Decision trees can use `graph TD` with diamond decision nodes.

**`stateDiagram-v2` label caveat:** Transition labels have a strict parser — colons, parentheses, `
`, HTML entities, and most special characters cause silent parse failures ("Syntax error in text"). If your labels need any of these (e.g., `cancel()`, `curate: true`, multi-line labels), use `flowchart TD` instead with rounded nodes and quoted edge labels (`|"label text"|`). Flowcharts handle all special characters and support `
` for line breaks. Reserve `stateDiagram-v2` for simple single-word or plain-text labels.

### Mind Maps / Hierarchical Breakdowns
**Use Mermaid.** Use `mindmap` syntax for hierarchical branching from a root node. Mermaid handles the radial layout automatically. Style with `themeVariables` to control node colors at each depth level.

### Class Diagrams
**Use Mermaid.** Use `classDiagram` syntax for domain modeling, OOP design, and entity relationships with typed properties and methods. Supports relationships: association (`-->`), composition (`*--`), aggregation (`o--`), and inheritance (`<|--`). Add multiplicity labels (e.g., `"1" --> "*"`) and abstract/interface markers (`<>`, `<>`). For simple entity boxes without OOP semantics (no methods, no inheritance), prefer `erDiagram` instead — it produces cleaner output for pure data modeling.

### C4 Architecture Diagrams
**Use Mermaid flowchart syntax — NOT native C4.** Use `graph TD` with `subgraph` blocks for C4 boundaries. Native `C4Context` hardcodes sharp corners, its own font, blue icons, and inline SVG colors that ignore `themeVariables` — it always clashes with custom palettes.

**Flowchart-as-C4 pattern:** Persons → rounded nodes `(("Name"))`, systems → rectangles `["Name"]`, databases → cylinders `[("Name")]`, boundaries → `subgraph` blocks, relationships → labeled arrows `-->|"protocol"|`. import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as ticker
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, FancyArrowPatch
import numpy as np
import json

# ── Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

lcoe_data       = data['lcoe_trends']['data']
fossil_data     = data['fossil_fuel_lcoe_range']['data']
capacity_data   = data['installed_capacity']['data']
subsidy_data    = data['fossil_fuel_subsidies']['data']

# Extract vectors
years       = np.array([d['year'] for d in lcoe_data])
solar_lcoe  = np.array([d['solar_pv'] for d in lcoe_data])
wind_lcoe   = np.array([d['onshore_wind'] for d in lcoe_data])
battery_lcoe= np.array([d['battery_storage'] for d in lcoe_data])

yf          = np.array([d['year'] for d in fossil_data])
gas_low     = np.array([d['gas_ccgt_low'] for d in fossil_data])
gas_high    = np.array([d['gas_ccgt_high'] for d in fossil_data])
coal_low    = np.array([d['coal_low'] for d in fossil_data])
coal_high   = np.array([d['coal_high'] for d in fossil_data])

yc          = np.array([d['year'] for d in capacity_data])
solar_gw    = np.array([d['solar_pv_gw'] for d in capacity_data])
wind_gw     = np.array([d['onshore_wind_gw'] for d in capacity_data])

ys          = np.array([d['year'] for d in subsidy_data])
total_sub   = np.array([d['total_subsidies_bn'] for d in subsidy_data])
cons_sub    = np.array([d['consumption_subsidies_bn'] for d in subsidy_data])
prod_sub    = np.array([d['production_subsidies_bn'] for d in subsidy_data])

# Interpolate fossil range to all years for smooth band
fossil_low_all  = np.interp(years, yf, coal_low)
fossil_high_all = np.interp(years, yf, coal_high)

# ── Style ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family':     'DejaVu Serif',
    'font.size':       10,
    'axes.titlesize':  12,
    'axes.labelsize':  10,
    'xtick.labelsize': 9,
    'ytick.labelsize': 9,
    'legend.fontsize': 9,
    'figure.dpi':      200,
    'savefig.bbox':    'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.2,
})

# Color palette — editorial / publication-ready
C_SOLAR   = '#D4780A'   # warm amber
C_WIND    = '#2B6F9C'   # muted steel blue
C_BATTERY = '#C44E52'   # dusty rose/terracotta
C_SUBSIDY_FILL  = '#7B6B5D'  # warm brown
C_SUBSIDY_LINE  = '#4A3F35'  # dark brown
C_FOSSIL_BAND   = '#B0B0B0'  # mid gray
C_GRID      = '#E0E0E0'
C_ANNOT     = '#333333'

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10.5, 15))
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#FAFAF9')

# Create gridspec layout
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 1, hspace=0.35, height_ratios=[1.05, 0.90, 0.85],
                      left=0.10, right=0.95, top=0.96, bottom=0.04)

ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0])
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1])
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2])

# ── Helper: subtle grid & spine cleanup ────────────────────────────────
def style_ax(ax):
    ax.set_facecolor('#FAFAF9')
    ax.grid(True, color=C_GRID, linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.7)
    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['left'].set_color('#CCCCCC')
    ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('#CCCCCC')
    ax.tick_params(colors='#555555')

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PANEL 1 — LCOE Trends with Fossil Fuel Band
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ax1.fill_between(years, fossil_low_all, fossil_high_all,
                 color=C_FOSSIL_BAND, alpha=0.22, linewidth=0,
                 label='New fossil fuel cost range\n(coal low – coal high)')

l1, = ax1.plot(years, solar_lcoe,  color=C_SOLAR,   linewidth=2.0, marker='o',
               markersize=4.5, markevery=1, markerfacecolor='white',
               markeredgewidth=1.5, markeredgecolor=C_SOLAR,
               label='Solar PV (utility-scale)', zorder=5)
l2, = ax1.plot(years, wind_lcoe,   color=C_WIND,    linewidth=2.0, marker='s',
               markersize=4.0, markevery=1, markerfacecolor='white',
               markeredgewidth=1.5, markeredgecolor=C_WIND,
               label='Onshore wind', zorder=5)
l3, = ax1.plot(years, battery_lcoe, color=C_BATTERY, linewidth=2.0, marker='D',
               markersize=4.0, markevery=1, markerfacecolor='white',
               markeredgewidth=1.5, markeredgecolor=C_BATTERY,
               label='Battery storage (4-hr Li-ion)', zorder=4)

ax1.set_yscale('log')
ax1.set_ylabel('LCOE  (2023 USD / MWh, log scale)')
ax1.set_ylim(25, 1400)

# Crossover annotations
# Wind crossover: in 2016, wind=$56 < coal_low=$60
ax1.annotate('Onshore wind falls below\nnew coal cost (~2016)',
             xy=(2016, 56), xytext=(2011.5, 140),
             fontsize=7.5, color='#2B6F9C',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#2B6F9C', lw=1.0,
                             connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.1'),
             bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.35', facecolor='white',
                       edgecolor='#2B6F9C', alpha=0.85, linewidth=0.8),
             zorder=10)

# Solar crossover: in 2018, solar=$60, coal_low=$62
ax1.annotate('Solar PV falls below\nnew coal cost (~2018)',
             xy=(2018, 60), xytext=(2020.5, 130),
             fontsize=7.5, color='#B0680A',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#B0680A', lw=1.0,
                             connectionstyle='arc3,rad=-0.15'),
             bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.35', facecolor='white',
                       edgecolor='#B0680A', alpha=0.85, linewidth=0.8),
             zorder=10)

# Battery collapse annotation
ax1.annotate('Battery storage:\n$1,100 → $102/MWh\n(−91% decline)',
             xy=(2024, 102), xytext=(2017, 550),
             fontsize=7.5, color='#9E3E42',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#9E3E42', lw=1.0,
                             connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.2'),
             bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.35', facecolor='white',
                       edgecolor='#9E3E42', alpha=0.85, linewidth=0.8),
             zorder=10)

style_ax(ax1)
ax1.legend(loc='upper right', frameon=True, framealpha=0.9,
           edgecolor='#DDDDDD', fontsize=8, ncol=1)
ax1.set_title('Panel A — Levelized Cost of Energy: Renewables vs. Fossil Fuel Range (2010–2024)',
              fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', pad=8, loc='left', color='#222222')

# Custom y-ticks for log scale
ax1.yaxis.set_major_formatter(ticker.ScalarFormatter())
ax1.set_yticks([30, 40, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300, 500, 750, 1200])
ax1.set_yticklabels(['30', '40', '50', '75', '100', '150', '200', '300', '500', '750', '1,200'])

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PANEL 2 — Installed Capacity
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ax2.fill_between(yc, 0, solar_gw, color=C_SOLAR, alpha=0.30, linewidth=0)
ax2.plot(yc, solar_gw, color=C_SOLAR, linewidth=2.2, marker='o',
         markersize=4.5, markerfacecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1.5,
         markeredgecolor=C_SOLAR, label='Solar PV', zorder=5)

ax2.fill_between(yc, 0, wind_gw, color=C_WIND, alpha=0.25, linewidth=0)
ax2.plot(yc, wind_gw, color=C_WIND, linewidth=2.2, marker='s',
         markersize=4.0, markerfacecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1.5,
         markeredgecolor=C_WIND, label='Onshore wind', zorder=5)

# Highlight post-2018 acceleration zone
ax2.axvspan(2018, 2024.5, color=C_SOLAR, alpha=0.06, linewidth=0, zorder=0)
ax2.annotate('Post-2018\nsolar acceleration',
             xy=(2021.5, 1650), fontsize=8, color='#B0680A',
             fontstyle='italic', ha='center',
             bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white',
                       edgecolor='#DDDDDD', alpha=0.8))

ax2.set_ylabel('Cumulative installed capacity  (GW)')
ax2.set_ylim(0, 2250)
style_ax(ax2)
ax2.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, framealpha=0.9,
           edgecolor='#DDDDDD', fontsize=8)
ax2.set_title('Panel B — Cumulative Global Installed Capacity (2010–2024)',
              fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', pad=8, loc='left', color='#222222')

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PANEL 3 — Fossil Fuel Subsidies
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ax3.fill_between(ys, 0, prod_sub, color='#B8A99A', alpha=0.7, linewidth=0,
                 label='Production subsidies')
ax3.fill_between(ys, prod_sub, total_sub, color='#7B6B5D', alpha=0.8, linewidth=0,
                 label='Consumption subsidies')
ax3.plot(ys, total_sub, color=C_SUBSIDY_LINE, linewidth=2.0, marker='o',
         markersize=4.5, markerfacecolor=C_SUBSIDY_LINE, markeredgewidth=0,
         label='Total subsidies', zorder=5)

# 2022 energy crisis annotation
ax3.annotate('2022 energy\nprice crisis spike',
             xy=(2022, 700), xytext=(2018, 670),
             fontsize=7.5, color='#4A3F35',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#7B6B5D', lw=1.0,
                             connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.1'),
             bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.35', facecolor='white',
                       edgecolor='#7B6B5D', alpha=0.85, linewidth=0.8),
             zorder=10)

ax3.set_ylabel('Billion USD (nominal)')
ax3.set_xlabel('Year')
ax3.set_ylim(0, 820)
style_ax(ax3)
ax3.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, framealpha=0.9,
           edgecolor='#DDDDDD', fontsize=8, ncol=2)
ax3.set_title('Panel C — Global Fossil Fuel Subsidies: Consumption & Production (2010–2024)',
              fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', pad=8, loc='left', color='#222222')

# Shared x-axis
ax3.set_xticks(range(2010, 2025, 2))
ax3.set_xlim(2009.6, 2024.4)

# ── Super-title ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig.suptitle('The Renewable Energy Cost Revolution, 2010–2024',
             fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', x=0.10, ha='left', y=0.985,
             color='#111111')
fig.text(0.10, 0.970, 'Declining costs, surging deployment, and the persistence of fossil fuel subsidies',
         fontsize=10, color='#555555', ha='left', style='italic')

# ── Source footnote ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig.text(0.10, 0.005, 'Sources: LCOE data from IRENA / BloombergNEF; fossil fuel range illustrative estimates; '
         'subsidy data from IEA / IMF; 2024 values are preliminary. All LCOE in 2023 real USD.',
         fontsize=6.5, color='#999999', ha='left')

# ── Save ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import os
os.makedirs('/app/output', exist_ok=True)
fig.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, facecolor='#FAFAF9', edgecolor='none')
plt.close(fig)
